Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. God the Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away, Mujahid said: It is pulled away. As-Suddi said: It is uncovered. Ad-Dahhak said: It is scraped away and goes away. God the Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze, As-Suddi said: It is blazing hot. Qatadah said: It is kindled. He said: It is only set ablaze by the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when Paradise is brought near, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: meaning, it is brought near to its people. And the saying of God the Almighty: A soul will know what it has brought, this is the answer, meaning, when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it has done and what it has brought about for it, as God the Almighty said: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance. And God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: When When the sun is wrapped up was revealed, Umar said: When he reached A soul will know what it has brought, he said: This is why he included the hadith.
81:9: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the sun is wrapped up means it becomes dark. Al-Awfi said on his authority: it goes away. Mujahid said: it fades away and disappears. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Qatada said: its light goes away. Saeed bin Jubair said: it is wrapped up and disappears. Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: Kurrat means thrown. Abu Salih said: Kurrat means thrown. He also said: Naksat. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It falls to the ground. Ibn Jarir said: The correct statement in our view is that “takwir means gathering something together, and from this is the folding of a turban and gathering some clothes together. So the meaning of the words of God the Most High: Kurrat is gathering some of it together, then rolling it up and throwing it. And if that is done to it, its light will go away.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: “Abu Sa’id al-Ashja’ and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of a sheikh from Bajila, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “When the sun is wrapped up,” meaning that God will wrap the sun, moon, and stars in the sea on the Day of Resurrection, and God will send a violent wind that will set them ablaze with fire.” Aamer al-Sha’bi said the same. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: “My father told us, Abu Salih told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the words of God the Most High: “When the sun is wrapped up,” he said: Wrapped up in Hell. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa bin Muhammad bin Hibban told us, Darast bin Ziyad told us, Yazid al-Raqashi told us, Anas told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights that are barred in the Fire. This is a weak hadith because Yazid al-Raqashi is weak, and what al-Bukhari narrated in Sahih without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said: Musaddad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, Abdullah al-Danaaj told us, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and this is its wording. Rather, he included it in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, and it would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or repeat it, as was his custom in similar works. Al-Bazzar narrated it and he presented it well, so he said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad al-Baghdadi told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Danaaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman bin Khalid bin Abdullah al-Qasri in this mosque, the mosque of Kufa, and al-Hasan came and sat down. To him, so he narrated. He said: Abu Hurairah narrated to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire, barren on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: And what is their sin? He said: “I narrate to you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say:” I think he said: And what is their sin? Then he said: It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except through this chain of transmission, and Abdullah Ad-Danaaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah other than this hadith. And the Almighty said: "And when the stars are scattered" meaning they are scattered, as the Almighty said: "And when the stars are scattered. The root of inkadar is pouring out." Al-Rabi' bin Anas said, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: Six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are like that, the stars are scattered. While they are like that, the mountains fall on the face of the earth and move, shake, and mix, so the jinn flee to the humans and the humans flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals mix and swarm among themselves. "And when the wild animals are gathered together" He said: They are mixed. "And when the ten-year-olds are neglected" He said: Their people neglect them. "And when the seas are set ablaze" He said: The jinn will say, "We bring you report." He said: They set out to the sea, and behold, it is a blazing fire. He said: While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh lowest earth and up to the seventh highest heaven. He said: While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, and by Ibn Abi Hatim, with some of it. This is what Mujahid, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Ad-Dahhak said about the statement of God, the Most High: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are scattered. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam said on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And when the stars are scattered, he said: “They are scattered in Hell, and everyone who is worshipped other than God will be in Hell, except for Jesus and his mother. If they had been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with the chain of transmission mentioned above. And the Almighty said: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning they are removed from their places and blown away, leaving the earth a flat, barren plain. And His saying: And when the ten camels are neglected, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The ten camels. Mujahid said: They are neglected, they are left alone. Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak said: Their owners neglected them. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: They were not milked or milked, their owners abandoned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were left without a shepherd. The meaning of all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the ‘ashar camels, which are the best of them and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy – the singular is ‘ashra’ and that is its name until they give birth – people have become busy with them and with their care and benefit from them after they had desired nothing from them because of the great, terrifying, and awesome matter that has befallen them, which is the matter of the Day of Resurrection and the establishment of its causes and the occurrence of its preliminaries. And it has been said that it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and their owners will see them like that, with no way to them. And it has been said about the ‘ashar that they are the clouds that are neglected from traveling between the sky and the earth because of the destruction of the world. And it has been said that they are The land subject to tithe. It was also said that it refers to the homes that were inhabited and were abandoned due to the death of their inhabitants. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi narrated all of these sayings in his book Al-Tadhkira. He preferred that it refers to camels and attributed this to most people. I said: Nothing is known from the Salaf and the Imams other than this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means they are gathered as the Almighty said: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Register. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.” Ibn Abbas said: Everything will be gathered together, even flies. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, al-Suddi, and others said. This is what Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: These creatures will meet and God will decree for them what He wills. Ikrimah said: He will gather them for their death. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together he said: The beasts will be gathered for their death, and everything will be gathered for death except the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim. And when the wild beasts are gathered together means: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: He said: My father mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Its death will gather it. It was previously reported from Abi bin Ka’b that he said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means mixed together. Ibn Jarir said: The first statement is that of the one who said: Its gathered together. God Almighty said: And the birds are gathered together meaning gathered together. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I do not think he is anything but truthful. And the set ablaze sea. And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Abbas and others said: God sends raging winds upon them, which set them ablaze and they become a blazing fire. We have already discussed this in the statement of God the Almighty: And the set ablaze sea. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me – a righteous sheikh who resembles Malik ibn Anas – from Mu’awiyah ibn Sa’id, who said: Indeed, this sea is a pool – meaning the Roman Sea – in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers flow into it, and the Great Sea flows into it, and below it are wells covered with copper. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be set ablaze.” This is a strange and amazing report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: No one shall board the sea except a pilgrim, a performer of Umrah, or a warrior, for beneath the sea is a fire, and beneath the fire is a sea. This has been discussed previously in Surat Fatir. Mujahid and Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: It was lit or kindled. Al-Hasan said: It dried up. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Its water subsided and disappeared, so not a drop remained in it. Ad-Dahhak also said: It was lit or made to gush forth. As-Suddi said: It was opened and made to flow. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: It was lit or overflowed. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the souls are paired means gathering each type with its counterpart, as the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when the souls are paired - he said: The pairs, each man with each people who used to do his work. That is because God, the Almighty, says: “And you were three types. * The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” He said: They are the pairs. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir that Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people and recited: And when the souls are paired. He said: Its pairing is that it unites every group with its group. And in another narration, they are the two men who do a deed and because of it they enter Paradise or Hell. And in a narration on the authority of al-Nu’man, he said: Umar was asked about the Almighty’s saying: “And when "The souls are paired." He said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man, and a bad man will be paired with a bad man in the Fire. This is the pairing of souls. In a narration from Al-Nu'man, Umar said to the al-Nas 114:What do you say in interpreting this verse: "And when souls are paired?" They remained silent. He said: But I know that a man will marry his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man will marry his counterpart from the people of the Fire. Then he recited: "Gather together those who did wrong and their mates." Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: "And when souls are paired," he said that this is when people will be in three mates. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid: "And when souls are paired," he said: And similar people are grouped together. This is what Al-Rabi' bin Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is the correct one. Another saying on the words of God the Almighty: “And when the souls are paired,” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Sarar, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A valley will flow from the base of the Throne with water between the two shouts, and the distance between them will be forty years, and from it will sprout every decayed creature, from humans, birds, and animals. If someone who had known them before that had passed by them, he would have recognized them on the face of the earth having grown. Then the souls will be sent forth and will mate the bodies, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, and this is what Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, meaning paired with the bodies. It was said: The believers will be paired with the houris and the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. Al-Qurtubi related this in Al-Tadhkira. God the Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? This is how the majority read it: She will be asked. The girl buried alive is the one who the people of ignorance used to bury in the ground because they hated daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the girl buried alive will be asked for what sin she was killed, as a threat to her killer. If the wronged person is asked, what will the wrongdoer think then? Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the girl buried alive is asked, meaning asked. Abu al-Dhaha said the same: asked, meaning her blood was demanded. Al-Suddi and Qatadah narrated something similar. There are hadiths related to the female infant buried alive. Imam Ahmad said: “Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Abu Al-Aswad, who is Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Jadhamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukasha, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, among some people and he was saying: ‘I was thinking of forbidding Ghaylah, but I looked at the Romans and Persians and I saw that they bury their children alive without it harming them at all.’ Then they asked him about coitus interruptus coitus interruptus. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is the hidden burying alive, and that is the female infant buried alive. I was asked.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri, who is Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub. Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub. Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, all three of them on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “O Messenger of God, our mother Malikah used to maintain family ties, entertain guests, and do other good deeds. She died in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: No. We said: “She also buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire, unless the one who buries a child embraces Islam and then God forgives her. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah and Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire. Ahmad also said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, Aouf told us, Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah Al-Suraymiyyah told me, on the authority of her uncle, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the one who is born is in Paradise, and the girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Qurrah told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: It was said, O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. This is a mursal hadith from Al-Hasan and others before him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The children of the polytheists are in Paradise, so whoever claims that they are in Hell has lied. God Almighty says: And when the girl buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? Ibn Abbas said: It is the one who is buried. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, he said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I buried my daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. He said: Free a slave for each one of them. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: Then slaughter a camel for each one of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abd al-Razzaq disagreed with him on this matter, and he only wrote it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Mahdi on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us in what he wrote to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly, except that he said: Eight daughters of mine were buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. And at the end of it he said: Then sacrifice, if you wish, a camel for each one. Then he said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: O Messenger of God, I buried twelve or thirteen daughters alive during the pre-Islamic period. He said: Free the number of them. He said: So he freed the number of them. Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: So we rested her and called her Al-Qaisiyyah. And the Almighty said: And when the records are spread out. Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. If they had been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with the chain of transmission mentioned above. And the Almighty said: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning they are removed from their places and blown away, leaving the earth a flat, barren plain. And His saying: And when the ten camels are neglected, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The ten camels. Mujahid said: They are neglected, they are left alone. Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak said: Their owners neglected them. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: They were not milked or milked, their owners abandoned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were left without a shepherd. The meaning of all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the ‘ashar camels, which are the best of them and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy – the singular is ‘ashra’ and that is its name until they give birth – people have become busy with them and with their care and benefit from them after they had desired nothing from them because of the great, terrifying, and awesome matter that has befallen them, which is the matter of the Day of Resurrection and the establishment of its causes and the occurrence of its preliminaries. And it has been said that it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and their owners will see them like that, with no way to them. And it has been said about the ‘ashar that they are the clouds that are neglected from traveling between the sky and the earth because of the destruction of the world. And it has been said that they are The land subject to tithe. It was also said that it refers to the homes that were inhabited and were abandoned due to the death of their inhabitants. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi narrated all of these sayings in his book Al-Tadhkira. He preferred that it refers to camels and attributed this to most people. I said: Nothing is known from the Salaf and the Imams other than this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means they are gathered as the Almighty said: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Register. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.” Ibn Abbas said: Everything will be gathered together, even flies. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, al-Suddi, and others said. This is what Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: These creatures will meet and God will decree for them what He wills. Ikrimah said: He will gather them for their death. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together he said: The beasts will be gathered for their death, and everything will be gathered for death except the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim. And when the wild beasts are gathered together means: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: He said: My father mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Its death will gather it. It was previously reported from Abi bin Ka’b that he said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means mixed together. Ibn Jarir said: The first statement is that of the one who said: Its gathered together. God Almighty said: And the birds are gathered together meaning gathered together. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I do not think he is anything but truthful. And the set ablaze sea. And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Abbas and others said: God sends raging winds upon them, which set them ablaze and they become a blazing fire. We have already discussed this in the statement of God the Almighty: And the set ablaze sea. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me – a righteous sheikh who resembles Malik ibn Anas – from Mu’awiyah ibn Sa’id, who said: Indeed, this sea is a pool – meaning the Roman Sea – in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers flow into it, and the Great Sea flows into it, and below it are wells covered with copper. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be set ablaze.” This is a strange and amazing report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: No one shall board the sea except a pilgrim, a performer of Umrah, or a warrior, for beneath the sea is a fire, and beneath the fire is a sea. This has been discussed previously in Surat Fatir. Mujahid and Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: It was lit or kindled. Al-Hasan said: It dried up. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Its water subsided and disappeared, so not a drop remained in it. Ad-Dahhak also said: It was lit or made to gush forth. As-Suddi said: It was opened and made to flow. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: It was lit or overflowed. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the souls are paired means gathering each type with its counterpart, as the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when the souls are paired - he said: The pairs, each man with each people who used to do his work. That is because God, the Almighty, says: “And you were three types. * The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” He said: They are the pairs. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir that Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people and recited: And when the souls are paired. He said: Its pairing is that it unites every group with its group. And in another narration, they are the two men who do a deed and because of it they enter Paradise or Hell. And in a narration on the authority of al-Nu’man, he said: Umar was asked about the Almighty’s saying: “And when The souls are paired. He said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man, and a bad man will be paired with a bad man in the Fire. This is the pairing of souls. In a narration from Al-Nu'man, Umar said to the al-Nas 114:What do you say in interpreting this verse: And when souls are paired? They remained silent. He said: But I know that a man will marry his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man will marry his counterpart from the people of the Fire. Then he recited: Gather together those who did wrong and their mates. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: And when souls are paired, he said that this is when people will be in three mates. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid: And when souls are paired, he said: And similar people are grouped together. This is what Al-Rabi' bin Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is the correct one. Another saying on the words of God the Almighty: “And when the souls are paired,” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Sarar, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A valley will flow from the base of the Throne with water between the two shouts, and the distance between them will be forty years, and from it will sprout every decayed creature, from humans, birds, and animals. If someone who had known them before that had passed by them, he would have recognized them on the face of the earth having grown. Then the souls will be sent forth and will mate the bodies, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, and this is what Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, meaning paired with the bodies. It was said: The believers will be paired with the houris and the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. Al-Qurtubi related this in Al-Tadhkira. God the Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? This is how the majority read it: She will be asked. The girl buried alive is the one who the people of ignorance used to bury in the ground because they hated daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the girl buried alive will be asked for what sin she was killed, as a threat to her killer. If the wronged person is asked, what will the wrongdoer think then? Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the girl buried alive is asked, meaning asked. Abu al-Dhaha said the same: asked, meaning her blood was demanded. Al-Suddi and Qatadah narrated something similar. There are hadiths related to the female infant buried alive. Imam Ahmad said: “Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Abu Al-Aswad, who is Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Jadhamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukasha, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, among some people and he was saying: ‘I was thinking of forbidding Ghaylah, but I looked at the Romans and Persians and I saw that they bury their children alive without it harming them at all.’ Then they asked him about coitus interruptus coitus interruptus. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is the hidden burying alive, and that is the female infant buried alive. I was asked.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri, who is Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub. Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub. Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, all three of them on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “O Messenger of God, our mother Malikah used to maintain family ties, entertain guests, and do other good deeds. She died in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: No. We said: “She also buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire, unless the one who buries a child embraces Islam and then God forgives her. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah and Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire. Ahmad also said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, Aouf told us, Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah Al-Suraymiyyah told me, on the authority of her uncle, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the one who is born is in Paradise, and the girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Qurrah told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: It was said, O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. This is a mursal hadith from Al-Hasan and others before him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The children of the polytheists are in Paradise, so whoever claims that they are in Hell has lied. God Almighty says: And when the girl buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? Ibn Abbas said: It is the one who is buried. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, he said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I buried my daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. He said: Free a slave for each one of them. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: Then slaughter a camel for each one of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abd al-Razzaq disagreed with him on this matter, and he only wrote it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Mahdi on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us in what he wrote to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly, except that he said: Eight daughters of mine were buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. And at the end of it he said: Then sacrifice, if you wish, a camel for each one. Then he said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: O Messenger of God, I buried twelve or thirteen daughters alive during the pre-Islamic period. He said: Free the number of them. He said: So he freed the number of them. Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: So we rested her and called her Al-Qaisiyyah. And the Almighty said: And when the records are spread out. Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. God the Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away, Mujahid said: It is pulled away. As-Suddi said: It is uncovered. Ad-Dahhak said: It is scraped away and goes away. God the Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze, As-Suddi said: It is blazing hot. Qatadah said: It is kindled. He said: It is only set ablaze by the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when Paradise is brought near, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: meaning, it is brought near to its people. And the saying of God the Almighty: A soul will know what it has brought, this is the answer, meaning, when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it has done and what it has brought about for it, as God the Almighty said: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance. And God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: When When the sun is wrapped up was revealed, Umar said: When he reached A soul will know what it has brought, he said: This is why he included the hadith.
81:11: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the sun is wrapped up means it becomes dark. Al-Awfi said on his authority: it goes away. Mujahid said: it fades away and disappears. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Qatada said: its light goes away. Saeed bin Jubair said: it is wrapped up and disappears. Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: Kurrat means thrown. Abu Salih said: Kurrat means thrown. He also said: Naksat. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It falls to the ground. Ibn Jarir said: The correct statement in our view is that “takwir means gathering something together, and from this is the folding of a turban and gathering some clothes together. So the meaning of the words of God the Most High: Kurrat is gathering some of it together, then rolling it up and throwing it. And if that is done to it, its light will go away.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: “Abu Sa’id al-Ashja’ and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of a sheikh from Bajila, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “When the sun is wrapped up,” meaning that God will wrap the sun, moon, and stars in the sea on the Day of Resurrection, and God will send a violent wind that will set them ablaze with fire.” Aamer al-Sha’bi said the same. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: “My father told us, Abu Salih told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the words of God the Most High: “When the sun is wrapped up,” he said: Wrapped up in Hell. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa bin Muhammad bin Hibban told us, Darast bin Ziyad told us, Yazid al-Raqashi told us, Anas told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights that are barred in the Fire. This is a weak hadith because Yazid al-Raqashi is weak, and what al-Bukhari narrated in Sahih without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said: Musaddad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, Abdullah al-Danaaj told us, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and this is its wording. Rather, he included it in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, and it would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or repeat it, as was his custom in similar works. Al-Bazzar narrated it and he presented it well, so he said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad al-Baghdadi told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Danaaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman bin Khalid bin Abdullah al-Qasri in this mosque, the mosque of Kufa, and al-Hasan came and sat down. To him, so he narrated. He said: Abu Hurairah narrated to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire, barren on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: And what is their sin? He said: “I narrate to you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say:” I think he said: And what is their sin? Then he said: It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except through this chain of transmission, and Abdullah Ad-Danaaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah other than this hadith. And the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered meaning they are scattered, as the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered. The root of inkadar is pouring out. Al-Rabi' bin Anas said, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: Six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are like that, the stars are scattered. While they are like that, the mountains fall on the face of the earth and move, shake, and mix, so the jinn flee to the humans and the humans flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals mix and swarm among themselves. And when the wild animals are gathered together He said: They are mixed. And when the ten-year-olds are neglected He said: Their people neglect them. And when the seas are set ablaze He said: The jinn will say, We bring you report. He said: They set out to the sea, and behold, it is a blazing fire. He said: While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh lowest earth and up to the seventh highest heaven. He said: While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, and by Ibn Abi Hatim, with some of it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid: And when souls are paired, he said: And similar people are grouped together. This is what Al-Rabi' bin Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is the correct one. Another saying on the words of God the Almighty: “And when the souls are paired,” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Sarar, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A valley will flow from the base of the Throne with water between the two shouts, and the distance between them will be forty years, and from it will sprout every decayed creature, from humans, birds, and animals. If someone who had known them before that had passed by them, he would have recognized them on the face of the earth having grown. Then the souls will be sent forth and will mate the bodies, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, and this is what Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, meaning paired with the bodies. It was said: The believers will be paired with the houris and the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. Al-Qurtubi related this in Al-Tadhkira. God the Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? This is how the majority read it: She will be asked. The girl buried alive is the one who the people of ignorance used to bury in the ground because they hated daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the girl buried alive will be asked for what sin she was killed, as a threat to her killer. If the wronged person is asked, what will the wrongdoer think then? Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the girl buried alive is asked, meaning asked. Abu al-Dhaha said the same: asked, meaning her blood was demanded. Al-Suddi and Qatadah narrated something similar. There are hadiths related to the female infant buried alive. Imam Ahmad said: “Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Abu Al-Aswad, who is Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Jadhamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukasha, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, among some people and he was saying: ‘I was thinking of forbidding Ghaylah, but I looked at the Romans and Persians and I saw that they bury their children alive without it harming them at all.’ Then they asked him about coitus interruptus coitus interruptus. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is the hidden burying alive, and that is the female infant buried alive. I was asked.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri, who is Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub. Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub. Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, all three of them on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “O Messenger of God, our mother Malikah used to maintain family ties, entertain guests, and do other good deeds. She died in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: No. We said: “She also buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire, unless the one who buries a child embraces Islam and then God forgives her. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah and Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire. Ahmad also said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, Aouf told us, Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah Al-Suraymiyyah told me, on the authority of her uncle, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the one who is born is in Paradise, and the girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Qurrah told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: It was said, O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. This is a mursal hadith from Al-Hasan and others before him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The children of the polytheists are in Paradise, so whoever claims that they are in Hell has lied. God Almighty says: And when the girl buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? Ibn Abbas said: It is the one who is buried. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, he said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I buried my daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. He said: Free a slave for each one of them. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: Then slaughter a camel for each one of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abd al-Razzaq disagreed with him on this matter, and he only wrote it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Mahdi on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us in what he wrote to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly, except that he said: Eight daughters of mine were buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. And at the end of it he said: Then sacrifice, if you wish, a camel for each one. Then he said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: O Messenger of God, I buried twelve or thirteen daughters alive during the pre-Islamic period. He said: Free the number of them. He said: So he freed the number of them. Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: So we rested her and called her Al-Qaisiyyah. And the Almighty said: And when the records are spread out. Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. God the Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away, Mujahid said: It is pulled away. As-Suddi said: It is uncovered. Ad-Dahhak said: It is scraped away and goes away. God the Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze, As-Suddi said: It is blazing hot. Qatadah said: It is kindled. He said: It is only set ablaze by the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when Paradise is brought near, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: meaning, it is brought near to its people. And the saying of God the Almighty: A soul will know what it has brought, this is the answer, meaning, when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it has done and what it has brought about for it, as God the Almighty said: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance. And God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: When When the sun is wrapped up was revealed, Umar said: When he reached A soul will know what it has brought, he said: This is why he included the hadith.
81:12: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the sun is wrapped up means it becomes dark. Al-Awfi said on his authority: it goes away. Mujahid said: it fades away and disappears. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Qatada said: its light goes away. Saeed bin Jubair said: it is wrapped up and disappears. Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: Kurrat means thrown. Abu Salih said: Kurrat means thrown. He also said: Naksat. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It falls to the ground. Ibn Jarir said: The correct statement in our view is that “takwir means gathering something together, and from this is the folding of a turban and gathering some clothes together. So the meaning of the words of God the Most High: Kurrat is gathering some of it together, then rolling it up and throwing it. And if that is done to it, its light will go away.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: “Abu Sa’id al-Ashja’ and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of a sheikh from Bajila, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “When the sun is wrapped up,” meaning that God will wrap the sun, moon, and stars in the sea on the Day of Resurrection, and God will send a violent wind that will set them ablaze with fire.” Aamer al-Sha’bi said the same. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: “My father told us, Abu Salih told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the words of God the Most High: “When the sun is wrapped up,” he said: Wrapped up in Hell. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa bin Muhammad bin Hibban told us, Darast bin Ziyad told us, Yazid al-Raqashi told us, Anas told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights that are barred in the Fire. This is a weak hadith because Yazid al-Raqashi is weak, and what al-Bukhari narrated in Sahih without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said: Musaddad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, Abdullah al-Danaaj told us, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and this is its wording. Rather, he included it in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, and it would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or repeat it, as was his custom in similar works. Al-Bazzar narrated it and he presented it well, so he said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad al-Baghdadi told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Danaaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman bin Khalid bin Abdullah al-Qasri in this mosque, the mosque of Kufa, and al-Hasan came and sat down. To him, so he narrated. He said: Abu Hurairah narrated to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire, barren on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: And what is their sin? He said: “I narrate to you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say:” I think he said: And what is their sin? Then he said: It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except through this chain of transmission, and Abdullah Ad-Danaaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah other than this hadith. And the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered meaning they are scattered, as the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered. The root of inkadar is pouring out. Al-Rabi' bin Anas said, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: Six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are like that, the stars are scattered. While they are like that, the mountains fall on the face of the earth and move, shake, and mix, so the jinn flee to the humans and the humans flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals mix and swarm among themselves. And when the wild animals are gathered together He said: They are mixed. And when the ten-year-olds are neglected He said: Their people neglect them. And when the seas are set ablaze He said: The jinn will say, We bring you report. He said: They set out to the sea, and behold, it is a blazing fire. He said: While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh lowest earth and up to the seventh highest heaven. He said: While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, and by Ibn Abi Hatim, with some of it. This is what Mujahid, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Ad-Dahhak said about the statement of God, the Most High: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are scattered. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam said on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And when the stars are scattered, he said: “They are scattered in Hell, and everyone who is worshipped other than God will be in Hell, except for Jesus and his mother. If they had been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with the chain of transmission mentioned above. And the Almighty said: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning they are removed from their places and blown away, leaving the earth a flat, barren plain. And His saying: And when the ten camels are neglected, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The ten camels. Mujahid said: They are neglected, they are left alone. Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak said: Their owners neglected them. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: They were not milked or milked, their owners abandoned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were left without a shepherd. The meaning of all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the ‘ashar camels, which are the best of them and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy – the singular is ‘ashra’ and that is its name until they give birth – people have become busy with them and with their care and benefit from them after they had desired nothing from them because of the great, terrifying, and awesome matter that has befallen them, which is the matter of the Day of Resurrection and the establishment of its causes and the occurrence of its preliminaries. And it has been said that it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and their owners will see them like that, with no way to them. And it has been said about the ‘ashar that they are the clouds that are neglected from traveling between the sky and the earth because of the destruction of the world. And it has been said that they are The land subject to tithe. It was also said that it refers to the homes that were inhabited and were abandoned due to the death of their inhabitants. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi narrated all of these sayings in his book Al-Tadhkira. He preferred that it refers to camels and attributed this to most people. I said: Nothing is known from the Salaf and the Imams other than this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means they are gathered as the Almighty said: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Register. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.” Ibn Abbas said: Everything will be gathered together, even flies. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, al-Suddi, and others said. This is what Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: These creatures will meet and God will decree for them what He wills. Ikrimah said: He will gather them for their death. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together he said: The beasts will be gathered for their death, and everything will be gathered for death except the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim. And when the wild beasts are gathered together means: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: He said: My father mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Its death will gather it. It was previously reported from Abi bin Ka’b that he said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means mixed together. Ibn Jarir said: The first statement is that of the one who said: Its gathered together. God Almighty said: And the birds are gathered together meaning gathered together. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I do not think he is anything but truthful. And the set ablaze sea. And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Abbas and others said: God sends raging winds upon them, which set them ablaze and they become a blazing fire. We have already discussed this in the statement of God the Almighty: And the set ablaze sea. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me – a righteous sheikh who resembles Malik ibn Anas – from Mu’awiyah ibn Sa’id, who said: Indeed, this sea is a pool – meaning the Roman Sea – in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers flow into it, and the Great Sea flows into it, and below it are wells covered with copper. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be set ablaze.” This is a strange and amazing report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: No one shall board the sea except a pilgrim, a performer of Umrah, or a warrior, for beneath the sea is a fire, and beneath the fire is a sea. This has been discussed previously in Surat Fatir. Mujahid and Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: It was lit or kindled. Al-Hasan said: It dried up. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Its water subsided and disappeared, so not a drop remained in it. Ad-Dahhak also said: It was lit or made to gush forth. As-Suddi said: It was opened and made to flow. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: It was lit or overflowed. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the souls are paired means gathering each type with its counterpart, as the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when the souls are paired - he said: The pairs, each man with each people who used to do his work.
