Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: So we rested her and called her Al-Qaisiyyah. And the Almighty said: And when the records are spread out. Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. God the Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away, Mujahid said: It is pulled away. As-Suddi said: It is uncovered. Ad-Dahhak said: It is scraped away and goes away. God the Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze, As-Suddi said: It is blazing hot. Qatadah said: It is kindled. He said: It is only set ablaze by the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when Paradise is brought near, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: meaning, it is brought near to its people. And the saying of God the Almighty: A soul will know what it has brought, this is the answer, meaning, when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it has done and what it has brought about for it, as God the Almighty said: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance. And God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: When When the sun is wrapped up was revealed, Umar said: When he reached A soul will know what it has brought, he said: This is why he included the hadith.
81:13: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the sun is wrapped up means it becomes dark. Al-Awfi said on his authority: it goes away. Mujahid said: it fades away and disappears. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Qatada said: its light goes away. Saeed bin Jubair said: it is wrapped up and disappears. Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: Kurrat means thrown. Abu Salih said: Kurrat means thrown. He also said: Naksat. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It falls to the ground. Ibn Jarir said: The correct statement in our view is that “takwir means gathering something together, and from this is the folding of a turban and gathering some clothes together. So the meaning of the words of God the Most High: Kurrat is gathering some of it together, then rolling it up and throwing it. And if that is done to it, its light will go away.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: “Abu Sa’id al-Ashja’ and Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of a sheikh from Bajila, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “When the sun is wrapped up,” meaning that God will wrap the sun, moon, and stars in the sea on the Day of Resurrection, and God will send a violent wind that will set them ablaze with fire.” Aamer al-Sha’bi said the same. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: “My father told us, Abu Salih told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the words of God the Most High: “When the sun is wrapped up,” he said: Wrapped up in Hell. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Musa bin Muhammad bin Hibban told us, Darast bin Ziyad told us, Yazid al-Raqashi told us, Anas told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights that are barred in the Fire. This is a weak hadith because Yazid al-Raqashi is weak, and what al-Bukhari narrated in Sahih without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said: Musaddad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, Abdullah al-Danaaj told us, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and this is its wording. Rather, he included it in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, and it would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or repeat it, as was his custom in similar works. Al-Bazzar narrated it and he presented it well, so he said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad al-Baghdadi told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Aziz bin al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Danaaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman bin Khalid bin Abdullah al-Qasri in this mosque, the mosque of Kufa, and al-Hasan came and sat down. To him, so he narrated. He said: Abu Hurairah narrated to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire, barren on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: And what is their sin? He said: “I narrate to you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say:” I think he said: And what is their sin? Then he said: It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except through this chain of transmission, and Abdullah Ad-Danaaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah other than this hadith. And the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered meaning they are scattered, as the Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered. The root of inkadar is pouring out. Al-Rabi' bin Anas said, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: Six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are like that, the stars are scattered. While they are like that, the mountains fall on the face of the earth and move, shake, and mix, so the jinn flee to the humans and the humans flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals mix and swarm among themselves. And when the wild animals are gathered together He said: They are mixed. And when the ten-year-olds are neglected He said: Their people neglect them. And when the seas are set ablaze He said: The jinn will say, We bring you report. He said: They set out to the sea, and behold, it is a blazing fire. He said: While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh lowest earth and up to the seventh highest heaven. He said: While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, and by Ibn Abi Hatim, with some of it. This is what Mujahid, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Ad-Dahhak said about the statement of God, the Most High: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are scattered. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam said on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And when the stars are scattered, he said: “They are scattered in Hell, and everyone who is worshipped other than God will be in Hell, except for Jesus and his mother. If they had been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with the chain of transmission mentioned above. And the Almighty said: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning they are removed from their places and blown away, leaving the earth a flat, barren plain. And His saying: And when the ten camels are neglected, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The ten camels. Mujahid said: They are neglected, they are left alone. Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak said: Their owners neglected them. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: They were not milked or milked, their owners abandoned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were left without a shepherd. The meaning of all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the ‘ashar camels, which are the best of them and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy – the singular is ‘ashra’ and that is its name until they give birth – people have become busy with them and with their care and benefit from them after they had desired nothing from them because of the great, terrifying, and awesome matter that has befallen them, which is the matter of the Day of Resurrection and the establishment of its causes and the occurrence of its preliminaries. And it has been said that it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and their owners will see them like that, with no way to them. And it has been said about the ‘ashar that they are the clouds that are neglected from traveling between the sky and the earth because of the destruction of the world. And it has been said that they are The land subject to tithe. It was also said that it refers to the homes that were inhabited and were abandoned due to the death of their inhabitants. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi narrated all of these sayings in his book Al-Tadhkira. He preferred that it refers to camels and attributed this to most people. I said: Nothing is known from the Salaf and the Imams other than this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means they are gathered as the Almighty said: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Register. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.” Ibn Abbas said: Everything will be gathered together, even flies. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, al-Suddi, and others said. This is what Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: These creatures will meet and God will decree for them what He wills. Ikrimah said: He will gather them for their death. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together he said: The beasts will be gathered for their death, and everything will be gathered for death except the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim. And when the wild beasts are gathered together means: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: He said: My father mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Its death will gather it. It was previously reported from Abi bin Ka’b that he said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means mixed together. Ibn Jarir said: The first statement is that of the one who said: Its gathered together. God Almighty said: And the birds are gathered together meaning gathered together. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I do not think he is anything but truthful. And the set ablaze sea. And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Abbas and others said: God sends raging winds upon them, which set them ablaze and they become a blazing fire. We have already discussed this in the statement of God the Almighty: And the set ablaze sea. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me – a righteous sheikh who resembles Malik ibn Anas – from Mu’awiyah ibn Sa’id, who said: Indeed, this sea is a pool – meaning the Roman Sea – in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers flow into it, and the Great Sea flows into it, and below it are wells covered with copper. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be set ablaze.” This is a strange and amazing report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: No one shall board the sea except a pilgrim, a performer of Umrah, or a warrior, for beneath the sea is a fire, and beneath the fire is a sea. This has been discussed previously in Surat Fatir. Mujahid and Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: It was lit or kindled. Al-Hasan said: It dried up. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Its water subsided and disappeared, so not a drop remained in it. Ad-Dahhak also said: It was lit or made to gush forth. As-Suddi said: It was opened and made to flow. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: It was lit or overflowed. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the souls are paired means gathering each type with its counterpart, as the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when the souls are paired - he said: The pairs, each man with each people who used to do his work. That is because God, the Almighty, says: “And you were three types. * The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” He said: They are the pairs. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir that Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people and recited: And when the souls are paired. He said: Its pairing is that it unites every group with its group. And in another narration, they are the two men who do a deed and because of it they enter Paradise or Hell. And in a narration on the authority of al-Nu’man, he said: Umar was asked about the Almighty’s saying: “And when The souls are paired. He said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man, and a bad man will be paired with a bad man in the Fire. This is the pairing of souls. In a narration from Al-Nu'man, Umar said to the al-Nas 114:What do you say in interpreting this verse: And when souls are paired? They remained silent. He said: But I know that a man will marry his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man will marry his counterpart from the people of the Fire. Then he recited: Gather together those who did wrong and their mates. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: And when souls are paired, he said that this is when people will be in three mates. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid: And when souls are paired, he said: And similar people are grouped together. This is what Al-Rabi' bin Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is the correct one. Another saying on the words of God the Almighty: “And when the souls are paired,” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Sarar, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A valley will flow from the base of the Throne with water between the two shouts, and the distance between them will be forty years, and from it will sprout every decayed creature, from humans, birds, and animals. If someone who had known them before that had passed by them, he would have recognized them on the face of the earth having grown. Then the souls will be sent forth and will mate the bodies, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, and this is what Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, meaning paired with the bodies. It was said: The believers will be paired with the houris and the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. Al-Qurtubi related this in Al-Tadhkira. God the Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? This is how the majority read it: She will be asked. The girl buried alive is the one who the people of ignorance used to bury in the ground because they hated daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the girl buried alive will be asked for what sin she was killed, as a threat to her killer. If the wronged person is asked, what will the wrongdoer think then? Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the girl buried alive is asked, meaning asked. Abu al-Dhaha said the same: asked, meaning her blood was demanded. Al-Suddi and Qatadah narrated something similar. There are hadiths related to the female infant buried alive. Imam Ahmad said: “Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Abu Al-Aswad, who is Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Jadhamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukasha, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, among some people and he was saying: ‘I was thinking of forbidding Ghaylah, but I looked at the Romans and Persians and I saw that they bury their children alive without it harming them at all.’ Then they asked him about coitus interruptus coitus interruptus. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is the hidden burying alive, and that is the female infant buried alive. I was asked.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri, who is Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub. Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub. Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, all three of them on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “O Messenger of God, our mother Malikah used to maintain family ties, entertain guests, and do other good deeds. She died in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: No. We said: “She also buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire, unless the one who buries a child embraces Islam and then God forgives her. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah and Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire. Ahmad also said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, Aouf told us, Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah Al-Suraymiyyah told me, on the authority of her uncle, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the one who is born is in Paradise, and the girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Qurrah told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: It was said, O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. This is a mursal hadith from Al-Hasan and others before him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The children of the polytheists are in Paradise, so whoever claims that they are in Hell has lied. God Almighty says: And when the girl buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? Ibn Abbas said: It is the one who is buried. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, he said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I buried my daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. He said: Free a slave for each one of them. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: Then slaughter a camel for each one of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abd al-Razzaq disagreed with him on this matter, and he only wrote it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Mahdi on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us in what he wrote to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly, except that he said: Eight daughters of mine were buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. And at the end of it he said: Then sacrifice, if you wish, a camel for each one. Then he said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: O Messenger of God, I buried twelve or thirteen daughters alive during the pre-Islamic period. He said: Free the number of them. He said: So he freed the number of them. Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. He said: While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording, and by Ibn Abi Hatim, with some of it. This is what Mujahid, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Ad-Dahhak said about the statement of God, the Most High: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are scattered. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam said on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And when the stars are scattered, he said: “They are scattered in Hell, and everyone who is worshipped other than God will be in Hell, except for Jesus and his mother. If they had been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with the chain of transmission mentioned above. And the Almighty said: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning they are removed from their places and blown away, leaving the earth a flat, barren plain. And His saying: And when the ten camels are neglected, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: The ten camels. Mujahid said: They are neglected, they are left alone. Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak said: Their owners neglected them. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: They were not milked or milked, their owners abandoned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were left without a shepherd. The meaning of all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the ‘ashar camels, which are the best of them and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy – the singular is ‘ashra’ and that is its name until they give birth – people have become busy with them and with their care and benefit from them after they had desired nothing from them because of the great, terrifying, and awesome matter that has befallen them, which is the matter of the Day of Resurrection and the establishment of its causes and the occurrence of its preliminaries. And it has been said that it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and their owners will see them like that, with no way to them. And it has been said about the ‘ashar that they are the clouds that are neglected from traveling between the sky and the earth because of the destruction of the world. And it has been said that they are The land subject to tithe. It was also said that it refers to the homes that were inhabited and were abandoned due to the death of their inhabitants. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Qurtubi narrated all of these sayings in his book Al-Tadhkira. He preferred that it refers to camels and attributed this to most people. I said: Nothing is known from the Salaf and the Imams other than this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means they are gathered as the Almighty said: “There is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Register. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.” Ibn Abbas said: Everything will be gathered together, even flies. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, al-Suddi, and others said. This is what Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: These creatures will meet and God will decree for them what He wills. Ikrimah said: He will gather them for their death. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: And when the wild beasts are gathered together he said: The beasts will be gathered for their death, and everything will be gathered for death except the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim. And when the wild beasts are gathered together means: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: He said: My father mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Its death will gather it. It was previously reported from Abi bin Ka’b that he said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together means mixed together. Ibn Jarir said: The first statement is that of the one who said: Its gathered together. God Almighty said: And the birds are gathered together meaning gathered together. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I do not think he is anything but truthful. And the set ablaze sea. And when the seas are set ablaze. Ibn Abbas and others said: God sends raging winds upon them, which set them ablaze and they become a blazing fire. We have already discussed this in the statement of God the Almighty: And the set ablaze sea. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me – a righteous sheikh who resembles Malik ibn Anas – from Mu’awiyah ibn Sa’id, who said: Indeed, this sea is a pool – meaning the Roman Sea – in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers flow into it, and the Great Sea flows into it, and below it are wells covered with copper. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be set ablaze.” This is a strange and amazing report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: No one shall board the sea except a pilgrim, a performer of Umrah, or a warrior, for beneath the sea is a fire, and beneath the fire is a sea. This has been discussed previously in Surat Fatir. Mujahid and Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: It was lit or kindled. Al-Hasan said: It dried up. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Its water subsided and disappeared, so not a drop remained in it. Ad-Dahhak also said: It was lit or made to gush forth. As-Suddi said: It was opened and made to flow. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: It was lit or overflowed. And the Almighty’s saying: And when the souls are paired means gathering each type with its counterpart, as the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And when the souls are paired - he said: The pairs, each man with each people who used to do his work. That is because God, the Almighty, says: “And you were three types. * The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” He said: They are the pairs. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir that Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people and recited: And when the souls are paired. He said: Its pairing is that it unites every group with its group. And in another narration, they are the two men who do a deed and because of it they enter Paradise or Hell. And in a narration on the authority of al-Nu’man, he said: Umar was asked about the Almighty’s saying: “And when The souls are paired. He said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man, and a bad man will be paired with a bad man in the Fire. This is the pairing of souls. In a narration from Al-Nu'man, Umar said to the al-Nas 114:What do you say in interpreting this verse: And when souls are paired? They remained silent. He said: But I know that a man will marry his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man will marry his counterpart from the people of the Fire. Then he recited: Gather together those who did wrong and their mates. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: And when souls are paired, he said that this is when people will be in three mates. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid: And when souls are paired, he said: And similar people are grouped together. This is what Al-Rabi' bin Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is the correct one. Another saying on the words of God the Almighty: “And when the souls are paired,” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Sarar, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A valley will flow from the base of the Throne with water between the two shouts, and the distance between them will be forty years, and from it will sprout every decayed creature, from humans, birds, and animals. If someone who had known them before that had passed by them, he would have recognized them on the face of the earth having grown. Then the souls will be sent forth and will mate the bodies, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, and this is what Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the souls are paired, meaning paired with the bodies. It was said: The believers will be paired with the houris and the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. Al-Qurtubi related this in Al-Tadhkira. God the Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? This is how the majority read it: She will be asked. The girl buried alive is the one who the people of ignorance used to bury in the ground because they hated daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the girl buried alive will be asked for what sin she was killed, as a threat to her killer. If the wronged person is asked, what will the wrongdoer think then? Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when the girl buried alive is asked, meaning asked. Abu al-Dhaha said the same: asked, meaning her blood was demanded. Al-Suddi and Qatadah narrated something similar. There are hadiths related to the female infant buried alive. Imam Ahmad said: “Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Abu Al-Aswad, who is Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Jadhamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukasha, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, among some people and he was saying: ‘I was thinking of forbidding Ghaylah, but I looked at the Romans and Persians and I saw that they bury their children alive without it harming them at all.’ Then they asked him about coitus interruptus coitus interruptus. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is the hidden burying alive, and that is the female infant buried alive. I was asked.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri, who is Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub. Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub. Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, all three of them on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: “O Messenger of God, our mother Malikah used to maintain family ties, entertain guests, and do other good deeds. She died in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: No. We said: “She also buried our sister alive in the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit her at all?” He said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire, unless the one who buries a child embraces Islam and then God forgives her. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah and Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who buries a child alive and the one who is buried alive are in Hellfire. Ahmad also said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, Aouf told us, Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah Al-Suraymiyyah told me, on the authority of her uncle, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the one who is born is in Paradise, and the girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Qurrah told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: It was said, O Messenger of God, who is in Paradise? He said: The girl who is buried alive is in Paradise. This is a mursal hadith from Al-Hasan and others before him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs ibn Umar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The children of the polytheists are in Paradise, so whoever claims that they are in Hell has lied. God Almighty says: And when the girl buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? Ibn Abbas said: It is the one who is buried. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, he said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I buried my daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. He said: Free a slave for each one of them. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: Then slaughter a camel for each one of them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abd al-Razzaq disagreed with him on this matter, and he only wrote it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Mahdi on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us in what he wrote to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission similarly, except that he said: Eight daughters of mine were buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. And at the end of it he said: Then sacrifice, if you wish, a camel for each one. Then he said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: O Messenger of God, I buried twelve or thirteen daughters alive during the pre-Islamic period. He said: Free the number of them. He said: So he freed the number of them. Then, the following year, he brought one hundred camels and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my people in response to what you did to the Muslims. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: So we rested her and called her Al-Qaisiyyah. And the Almighty said: And when the records are spread out. Ad-Dahhak said: Every person will be given his record in his right or left hand. Qatada said: O son of Adam, you fill out in it, then it is folded up and spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man consider what he fills out in his record. God the Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away, Mujahid said: It is pulled away. As-Suddi said: It is uncovered. Ad-Dahhak said: It is scraped away and goes away. God the Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze, As-Suddi said: It is blazing hot. Qatadah said: It is kindled. He said: It is only set ablaze by the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: And when Paradise is brought near, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: meaning, it is brought near to its people. And the saying of God the Almighty: A soul will know what it has brought, this is the answer, meaning, when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it has done and what it has brought about for it, as God the Almighty said: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance. And God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: When When the sun is wrapped up was revealed, Umar said: When he reached A soul will know what it has brought, he said: This is why he included the hadith.
81:15: Muslim narrated in his Sahih and An-Nasa'i in his Tafsir, regarding this verse, from the hadith of Mis'ar ibn Kadam, from Al-Walid ibn Sari', from Amr ibn Harith, who said: I prayed Fajr behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I heard him recite, So I swear by the stars that recede, * And the night when it darkens * And the morning when it breathes. An-Nasa'i narrated it from Bundar, from Ghandar, from Shu'bah, from Al-Hajjaj ibn Asim, from Abu Al-Aswad, from Amr ibn Harith, with a similar chain of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir said, through Ath-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from a man from Murad, from Ali, So I swear by the stars that recede, * And the stars that sweep away. He said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and appear at night. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us, from Samak ibn Harb, I heard Khalid ibn Arara, I heard Ali when he was asked about, I swear by the stars that recede, * And the stars that sweep away, and he said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and appear at night. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ali, who said: They are the stars. This is a good and authentic chain of transmission going back to Khalid ibn Arara, who is As-Sahmi Al-Kufi. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He narrated on the authority of Ali, and Samak and Al-Qasim ibn Auf Al-Shaibani narrated on his authority, and he did not mention any criticism or approval of him. And God knows best. Yunus narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali: They are the stars. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others that they are the stars. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Hudhah bin Khalifa told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah, regarding the verse: So I swear by the stars that recede, * The stars that move and clear. He said: They are the bright stars that run facing the east. Some of the imams said: The stars are called al-Khanas when they rise, then they are rans in their orbit, and when they set they are called kanas, from the Arab saying the gazelle retreats to its lair when it disappears into it. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah said: So I swear by al-Khanas he said: Wild cows. Ath-Thawri said the same on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Maysarah on the authority of Abdullah: So I swear by al-Khanas when they recede, The stars that move and clear. What are they, O Amr? I said: The cows. He said: And I see that. And thus Yunus narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of his father. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said on the authority of Amr on the authority of his father on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The cows sweep to the shade. And thus said Saeed bin Jubair. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are gazelles. And thus also said Saeed, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak. Abu Al-Sha’tha Jabir bin Zaid said: They are gazelles and cows. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told us, Hisham told us, Mughira told us on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid that they discussed this verse: So I swear by the receding stars, the sweeping stars. So Ibrahim said to Mujahid: Say what you heard about it. Mujahid said: We used to hear something about it and people say that they are the stars. So Ibrahim said: Say what you heard about it. He said: Mujahid said: We used to hear that they are the wild cows when they sweep in their rooms. So Ibrahim said: They are lying about Ali. This is as they narrated on the authority of Ali that he included the lower as the higher and the higher as the lower. Ibn Jarir hesitated about what was meant by his saying: The receding stars, the sweeping stars. Is it the stars or the gazelles and the wild cows? He said: It is possible that all of them are meant. And the Almighty’s saying: And the night when it covers has two opinions, one of them is that it approaches with its darkness. Mujahid said it becomes dark. Saeed bin Jubair said: When it arises. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: When it covers the people. And this is what Atiyah Al-Awfi said. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When it covers means when it turns away. And this is what Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak said. And this is what Zaid bin Aslam and his son Abd Al-Rahman said: When it covers means when it goes away. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu al-Buhturi who heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: Ali may God be pleased with him came out to us when the reward for the dawn prayer was due and said: Where are those who ask about the witr prayer? And the night when it covers with darkness * And the morning when it breathes This is when it has departed. Ibn Jarir preferred that what is meant by his saying When it covers with darkness is when it has departed. He said, according to his saying And the morning when it breathes meaning it has brightened, and he also cited as evidence the words of the poet: Until the morning breathes its breath and its night departs from it and darkens Any turning away, and I think that what is meant by His saying when it darkens is when it approaches, even though it is correct to use it to mean turning away as well, but approaching here is more appropriate, as if he swore by the night and its darkness when it approaches and by the dawn and its light when it shines, as God the Most High said: And the night when it covers * And the day when it appears Al-Anfal 1:17. And He the Most High said: And the forenoon * And the night when it covers Al-Anfal 1:17. And He the Most High said: And He who splits the dawn and makes the night for rest Al-Anfal 1:17, and other verses. Many of the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh said: The word ‘asaas is used to mean approaching and turning away in a shared manner, so based on this it is correct to mean both of them, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people who know the Arabic language claim that ‘asaas means that it drew near from the beginning and became dark. Al-Farra’ said: Abu al-Bilad the grammarian used to recite a verse. He could even spy on anyone if he wished to, and he could have a light source from it. He wants if he wishes, when it draws near, he would merge the dhal into the dal. Al-Farra’ said: They used to claim that this verse is fabricated. And the Almighty’s statement: And the morning when it breathes, Ad-Dahhak said: When it rises. Qatada said: When it lights up and approaches. Saeed bin Jubair said: When it arises, and this is what was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: It means the light of day when it approaches and becomes clear. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger means that this Qur’an is to convey a noble Messenger, that is, a noble angel of good character and splendid appearance, and he is Gabriel, peace be upon him. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Maymun ibn Mihran, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Al-Dahhak and others. Possessor of strength as in the Almighty’s saying: He taught him one of great strength, possessor of great power meaning, of great character, strong in strength and action. With the Lord of the Throne, secure meaning, he has a position with the Lord of the Throne, and a high status. Abu Salih said regarding the Almighty’s saying: With the Lord of the Throne, secure that Gabriel enters through seventy veils of light without permission. Obeyed then meaning, he has prestige and his speech is heard and obeyed in the highest assembly. Qatadah said, Obeyed then meaning, in the heavens, meaning, he is not one of the angels, but rather one of the masters and nobles, taken care of and chosen for this great message. And the Almighty’s saying: Trustworthy is an attribute of Gabriel with trustworthiness, and this is very great that the Lord Almighty purifies His servant and angelic messenger Gabriel as He purified His servant and human messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His Almighty’s saying: And your companion is not mad. Al-Sha’bi, Maymun bin Mihran, Abu Salih, and those mentioned above said: What is meant by His saying: And your companion is not mad is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the Almighty’s saying: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon means that Muhammad saw Gabriel, who brings him the message from God Almighty, in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings. On the clear horizon, meaning the clear one, and it is the first vision that was in Al-Batha’ and it is mentioned in His saying: “He was taught by one of great strength, possessing strength. So he rose up, while he was on the highest horizon. Then he drew near and came down, and was two bow lengths away or nearer. Then he revealed to His servant what He revealed,” as the explanation and explanation of that were presented. The evidence for that is that what is meant by that is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it appears, and God knows best, that this surah was revealed before the night of… Al-Isra’ because only this vision was mentioned in it, and it is the first. As for the second, which is mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: And he had certainly seen him in another descent * At the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge * When that which covered the Lote Tree covered it then that was only mentioned in Surat An-Najm and it was revealed after Surat Al-Isra’. God the Almighty says: And he is not stingy with regard to the unseen. Meaning, Muhammad is not suspicious of what God has revealed to him. Some of them read it with a Ḍad, meaning he is stingy, but rather he gives it to everyone. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Suspect and stingy are the same, meaning he is neither a liar nor a sinner. The suspect is the accused, and the stingy is the miser. Qatada said: The Qur’an was hidden, then God revealed it to Muhammad, and he did not withhold it from the people, but rather he spread it, conveyed it, and gave it to everyone who wanted it. This is what Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd, and others said. Ibn Jarir chose the reading of the letter Ḍād as I said. Both are mutawatir and their meaning is correct, as mentioned above. God the Almighty said: And it is not the word of an outcast devil. That is, this Qur’an is not the word of an outcast devil, meaning he is not able to carry it, nor is it appropriate for him, as God the Almighty said: “And the devils have not brought it down. Nor is it appropriate for them, nor are they able. Indeed, they are removed from hearing.” God the Almighty said: Then where do you go? That is, where do your minds go in your denial of this Qur’an, despite its clarity and obviousness, and its being the truth from God the Almighty, as Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to the delegation of Banu Hanifa when they came as Muslims, and he ordered them to recite to him some of the Qur’an of Musaylimah the Liar, which was at the height of delirium and weakness. He said: Woe to you, where do your minds go? By God, these words did not come from God, that is, from a god. Qatada said, So where are you going? That is, from the Book of God and from obeying Him. God the Almighty says: It is only a reminder to the worlds meaning this Qur'an is a reminder for all people so they may remember and be admonished by it. For whoever among you wills to go straight meaning whoever wants guidance should follow this Qur'an, for it is his salvation and guidance, and there is no guidance in anything else. And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds meaning the will is not left to you, so whoever wills will be guided and whoever wills will go astray. Rather, all of that is subject to the will of God the Almighty, Lord of the worlds. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir said, through Ath-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from a man from Murad, from Ali, So I swear by the stars that recede, * And the stars that sweep away. He said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and appear at night. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us, from Samak ibn Harb, I heard Khalid ibn Arara, I heard Ali when he was asked about, I swear by the stars that recede, * And the stars that sweep away, and he said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and appear at night. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ali, who said: They are the stars. This is a good and authentic chain of transmission going back to Khalid ibn Arara, who is As-Sahmi Al-Kufi. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He narrated on the authority of Ali, and Samak and Al-Qasim ibn Auf Al-Shaibani narrated on his authority, and he did not mention any criticism or approval of him. And God knows best. Yunus narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali: They are the stars. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others that they are the stars. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Hudhah bin Khalifa told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah, regarding the verse: So I swear by the stars that recede, * The stars that move and clear. He said: They are the bright stars that run facing the east. Some of the imams said: The stars are called al-Khanas when they rise, then they are rans in their orbit, and when they set they are called kanas, from the Arab saying the gazelle retreats to its lair when it disappears into it. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah said: So I swear by al-Khanas he said: Wild cows. Ath-Thawri said the same on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Maysarah on the authority of Abdullah: So I swear by al-Khanas when they recede, The stars that move and clear. What are they, O Amr? I said: The cows. He said: And I see that. And thus Yunus narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of his father. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said on the authority of Amr on the authority of his father on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The cows sweep to the shade. And thus said Saeed bin Jubair. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are gazelles. And thus also said Saeed, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak. Abu Al-Sha’tha Jabir bin Zaid said: They are gazelles and cows. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told us, Hisham told us, Mughira told us on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid that they discussed this verse: So I swear by the receding stars, the sweeping stars. So Ibrahim said to Mujahid: Say what you heard about it. Mujahid said: We used to hear something about it and people say that they are the stars. So Ibrahim said: Say what you heard about it. He said: Mujahid said: We used to hear that they are the wild cows when they sweep in their rooms. So Ibrahim said: They are lying about Ali. This is as they narrated on the authority of Ali that he included the lower as the higher and the higher as the lower. Ibn Jarir hesitated about what was meant by his saying: The receding stars, the sweeping stars. Is it the stars or the gazelles and the wild cows? He said: It is possible that all of them are meant. And the Almighty’s saying: And the night when it covers has two opinions, one of them is that it approaches with its darkness. Mujahid said it becomes dark. Saeed bin Jubair said: When it arises. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: When it covers the people. And this is what Atiyah Al-Awfi said. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When it covers means when it turns away. And this is what Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak said. And this is what Zaid bin Aslam and his son Abd Al-Rahman said: When it covers means when it goes away. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu al-Buhturi who heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: Ali may God be pleased with him came out to us when the reward for the dawn prayer was due and said: Where are those who ask about the witr prayer? And the night when it covers with darkness * And the morning when it breathes This is when it has departed. Ibn Jarir preferred that what is meant by his saying When it covers with darkness is when it has departed. He said, according to his saying And the morning when it breathes meaning it has brightened, and he also cited as evidence the words of the poet: Until the morning breathes its breath and its night departs from it and darkens Any turning away, and I think that what is meant by His saying when it darkens is when it approaches, even though it is correct to use it to mean turning away as well, but approaching here is more appropriate, as if he swore by the night and its darkness when it approaches and by the dawn and its light when it shines, as God the Most High said: And the night when it covers * And the day when it appears Al-Anfal 1:17. And He the Most High said: And the forenoon * And the night when it covers Al-Anfal 1:17. And He the Most High said: And He who splits the dawn and makes the night for rest Al-Anfal 1:17, and other verses. Many of the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh said: The word ‘asaas is used to mean approaching and turning away in a shared manner, so based on this it is correct to mean both of them, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people who know the Arabic language claim that ‘asaas means that it drew near from the beginning and became dark. Al-Farra’ said: Abu al-Bilad the grammarian used to recite a verse. He could even spy on anyone if he wished to, and he could have a light source from it. He wants if he wishes, when it draws near, he would merge the dhal into the dal. Al-Farra’ said: They used to claim that this verse is fabricated. And the Almighty’s statement: And the morning when it breathes, Ad-Dahhak said: When it rises. Qatada said: When it lights up and approaches. Saeed bin Jubair said: When it arises, and this is what was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: It means the light of day when it approaches and becomes clear. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger means that this Qur’an is to convey a noble Messenger, that is, a noble angel of good character and splendid appearance, and he is Gabriel, peace be upon him. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Maymun ibn Mihran, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Al-Dahhak and others. Possessor of strength as in the Almighty’s saying: He taught him one of great strength, possessor of great power meaning, of great character, strong in strength and action. With the Lord of the Throne, secure meaning, he has a position with the Lord of the Throne, and a high status. Abu Salih said regarding the Almighty’s saying: With the Lord of the Throne, secure that Gabriel enters through seventy veils of light without permission. Obeyed then meaning, he has prestige and his speech is heard and obeyed in the highest assembly. Qatadah said, Obeyed then meaning, in the heavens, meaning, he is not one of the angels, but rather one of the masters and nobles, taken care of and chosen for this great message. And the Almighty’s saying: Trustworthy is an attribute of Gabriel with trustworthiness, and this is very great that the Lord Almighty purifies His servant and angelic messenger Gabriel as He purified His servant and human messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His Almighty’s saying: And your companion is not mad. Then he revealed to His servant what He revealed,” as the explanation and explanation of that were presented. The evidence for that is that what is meant by that is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it appears, and God knows best, that this surah was revealed before the night of… Al-Isra’ because only this vision was mentioned in it, and it is the first. As for the second, which is mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: And he had certainly seen him in another descent * At the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge * When that which covered the Lote Tree covered it then that was only mentioned in Surat An-Najm and it was revealed after Surat Al-Isra’. Some of them read it with a Ḍad, meaning he is stingy, but rather he gives it to everyone. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Suspect and stingy are the same, meaning he is neither a liar nor a sinner. The suspect is the accused, and the stingy is the miser. This is what Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd, and others said. Ibn Jarir chose the reading of the letter Ḍād as I said. Both are mutawatir and their meaning is correct, as mentioned above. Obeyed then meaning, he has prestige and his speech is heard and obeyed in the highest assembly. Qatadah said, Obeyed then meaning, in the heavens, meaning, he is not one of the angels, but rather one of the masters and nobles, taken care of and chosen for this great message. And the Almighty’s saying: Trustworthy is an attribute of Gabriel with trustworthiness, and this is very great that the Lord Almighty purifies His servant and angelic messenger Gabriel as He purified His servant and human messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His Almighty’s saying: And your companion is not mad. Al-Sha’bi, Maymun bin Mihran, Abu Salih, and those mentioned above said: What is meant by His saying: And your companion is not mad is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ali, who said: They are the stars. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He narrated on the authority of Ali, and Samak and Al-Qasim ibn Auf Al-Shaibani narrated on his authority, and he did not mention any criticism or approval of him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir said, through Ath-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from a man from Murad, from Ali, So I swear by the stars that recede, * And the stars that sweep away. He said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and appear at night. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ali, who said: They are the stars. This is a good and authentic chain of transmission going back to Khalid ibn Arara, who is As-Sahmi Al-Kufi. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He narrated on the authority of Ali, and Samak and Al-Qasim ibn Auf Al-Shaibani narrated on his authority, and he did not mention any criticism or approval of him. And God knows best. Yunus narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali: They are the stars. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others that they are the stars. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Hudhah bin Khalifa told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah, regarding the verse: So I swear by the stars that recede, * The stars that move and clear. He said: They are the bright stars that run facing the east. Some of the imams said: The stars are called al-Khanas when they rise, then they are rans in their orbit, and when they set they are called kanas, from the Arab saying the gazelle retreats to its lair when it disappears into it. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah said: So I swear by al-Khanas he said: Wild cows. Ath-Thawri said the same on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Maysarah on the authority of Abdullah: So I swear by al-Khanas when they recede, The stars that move and clear. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said on the authority of Amr on the authority of his father on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The cows sweep to the shade. And this is what Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak said. And this is what Zaid bin Aslam and his son Abd Al-Rahman said: When it covers means when it goes away. Many of the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh said: The word ‘asaas is used to mean approaching and turning away in a shared manner, so based on this it is correct to mean both of them, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people who know the Arabic language claim that ‘asaas means that it drew near from the beginning and became dark. Al-Farra’ said: Abu al-Bilad the grammarian used to recite a verse. He could even spy on anyone if he wished to, and he could have a light source from it. Ibn Jarir said: It means the light of day when it approaches and becomes clear. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa: When this verse was revealed: For whoever among you wills to go straight Abu Jahl said: The matter is up to us: if we will, we will go straight, and if we will, we will not go straight. So God the Almighty revealed: And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds. The end of the interpretation of Surat At-Takwir. All praise and thanks are due to God.
